title: 2D pixel art generation with no/minimal third-party tools
author: Smart_Armadillo3472
selftext:
Hi folks, like many of you I'm dipping my toes into AI-led game development. I have zero coding skills, and minimal skill at visual art.

One of the most time-consuming parts for me has been pixel art asset generation. My goal thus far has been to avoid third-party tools such as Meshy, Tripo, or others, mainly because I don't want to pay for them, but also because I'm trying to future-proof my own setup and build things I need myself. I'm not going to pay for anything except my AI subscription at this stage.

To that end I've made a sprite workshop for editing sprites by hand myself, which works well. But the issue I keep coming up against is poor asset rendering (particularly with animations), even when using Fable 5.2! All the models seem to be able to recognise exactly what's wrong, and to be honest, my feedback is also extremely clear and detailed, but they just cannot get it right. Each new pass introduces a new weird visual glitch, so I feel like a dog chasing its tail right now.

So I guess my question is, is there anyone out there like me who is finding success doing it this way? If so, how?! Or alternatively, am I being a fool here and should I just bite the bullet and use more (free) online tools?

comments.author: RsetX
comments.body: https://shaddafare.itch.io/sprite-sheep this tool generate 2d animation with your GPU with a i2v and ref2v models, I added a pixel art feature

comments.author: stolenyourgf
comments.body: That 'dog chasing its tail' feeling is very common. Once a model pass is close, another generation often just trades one glitch for a new one — a color shift, a wobbling outline, or a feature that changes size. I'd stop iterating in the model when the silhouette and pose are readable, then finish in your sprite workshop: lock one palette for the whole sheet, remove anti-alias fringes and orphan pixels, and onion-skin the animation so the feet stay on a fixed pivot. If a new pass introduces a weird artifact, don't ask the model to 'fix this frame'; keep the previous rough and correct those pixels by hand. Treat the AI output as a rough, not a final asset.
